reading.body:
Gregory Meeks took $22,000 in AI company PAC money across 2025 and 2026 while sponsoring and cosponsoring AI export-control bills and voting for AI legislation.

The money is steady rather than dramatic. Eleven contributions between March 2025 and June 2026, from Amazon, Google, Meta, Microsoft, and Anthropic, ranging from $1,000 to $3,000. Amazon appears four times, Meta three, Google and Microsoft twice each, Anthropic once. No single contribution dominates, and the totals per company are small enough that no one funder stands out.

The legislative record runs in the same direction. Meeks sponsored the RESTRICT Act, which the data describes as covering export and security trade restrictions for integrated circuit technologies, and cosponsored the AI OVERWATCH Act on oversight of verified exports and restrictions on weaponizable advanced technology. Both are export-control bills, which is the part of AI policy that touches chips and the physical supply chain rather than model behavior. He also voted Yea on five bills, four of them in 2026.

What the data does not show is causation, and it does not claim any. Contributions and votes are listed in date order only. The page holds no committee assignments, no hearing record, no statements, and no explanation of what the five voted bills do. It also does not say whether the contributions came before or after any particular position, or whether the donors had business before Meeks. A reader can see that AI money and AI legislation both appear in one member's record. A reader cannot see from this data alone what either one did to the other.
